question: On 29 October 2023, the Israeli Ministry of Energy announced licences for natural gas exploration in maritime areas belonging to the State of Palestine1. These licences were granted to Dana Petroleum, Ratio Petroleum, ENI, BP, Azera Socar and NewMed Energy2. The licensed zones reportedly overlap with maritime areas declared by Palestine in 2019 under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea and the Oslo Accords.

Palestinian human rights organisations (Al-Haq, Al Mezan, PCHR, Adalah) have warned that these concessions may breach international humanitarian and customary law, including Article 55 of the Hague Regulations governing natural resources in occupied territories.

The exploitation of such resources by an occupying power constitutes a breach of international law, aggravates the conflict and sets a precedent for further de facto annexation. Paragraph 10 of the UN Economic and Social Council Resolution of 30 July 20253 reaffirms the ban on the economic exploitation of occupied territories such as the State of Palestine. In the light of this, can the Commission indicate: 1.
Whether it is aware of these concessions, their legal implications, and if it considers such acts to be compatible with the EU’s obligations under international law?
Whether it will consider a precautionary approach to the purchase of resources that may have been obtained while breaching international humanitarian and customary law?
Whether it will consider this issue in the assessment of measures towards Israel regarding confirmed violations of international humanitarian and customary law in Gaza?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.12.2025) The EU is aware of these gas explorations concessions and reiterates its strategic interest in a stable and secure environment in the Eastern Mediterranean. Regional cooperation in the Eastern Mediterranean must be developed in accordance with international law, including the United Nations (UN) Convention on the Law of the Sea.

The EU reaffirms its unwavering commitment to effective multilateralism and to the rulesbased international order with the UN at its core, steadfastly upholding the UN Charter and its rules and principles of sovereignty, territorial integrity, political independence and selfdetermination. Israel is bound by international humanitarian law (IHL) and applicable norms of international human rights law (IHRL).

The EU consistently calls on Israel to adhere strictly to the rules and principles of IHL and IHRL governing the use of force and the conduct of hostilities, including humanity, necessity, distinction and proportionality. The EU calls on Israel to ensure the impartial and effective investigation of alleged misconduct by the appropriate authorities in accordance with IHL.

In parallel, the Commission has proposed a package of measures, following the deterioration of the humanitarian situation in Gaza. These measures are still on the table of the Council, and the EU continues to maintain an open and frank dialogue with the Israeli government.
The EU stands ready to safeguard international law and international principles and is firmly committed to a lasting and sustainable peace based on the two-state solution.
